title: Safeguarding Your Finances: Spotting Income Tax Scams
description: Income Tax email and SMS scams are increasingly sophisticated, aiming to trick taxpayers into revealing sensitive financial information. Always verify the sen.

faq.q: How can I be certain an email is from the Income Tax Department?
faq.a: Always check the sender's email address for official domains like `@incometax.gov.in`. Look for personalised greetings, correct grammar, and ensure it doesn't ask for sensitive financial details or demand urgent action via a link.

faq.q: What should I do if I accidentally clicked a suspicious link?
faq.a: If you clicked a link but didn't enter any details, close the page immediately. If you did enter details, change your passwords for your e-filing account and bank accounts, and report the incident to the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.

faq.q: Will the Income Tax Department ever ask for my bank OTP or net banking password?
faq.a: No, the Income Tax Department will never ask for your bank account number, credit card details, UPI PIN, OTP, or net banking passwords via email, SMS, or phone call. Any such request is fraudulent.

faq.q: What types of attachments does the Income Tax Department send?
faq.a: The Income Tax Department typically sends attachments in PDF format for documents like intimation letters or assessment orders. They will never send executable files (.exe) or zipped files (.zip, .rar) as attachments.

faq.q: Where can I report an income tax scam?
faq.a: You can forward suspicious emails to `phishing@incometax.gov.in`. For more serious incidents or if you've lost money, file a complaint at the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal: `https://cybercrime.gov.in`.

faq.q: Can NRIs also be targeted by these scams?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs are equally vulnerable, especially if they are managing their Indian tax affairs remotely. The warning signs and protective measures apply universally to all Indian taxpayers.
